name: Zire
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page zire1240 (consulted 2026-09-17) and local Glottolog 5.1 sources.bib.
sources.note: No grammar, sketch or phonology is registered for Zire (Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology); the 1979 DEC volume 'Les langues mélanésiennes de Nouvelle-Calédonie' has notices for Ajië, Xârâcùù, extreme-south etc. but none for Sîchë.
No Sîshëë/Zire corpus; New Caledonian corpora present are Ajië, Bwatoo, Cèmuhî, Drehu, Fagauvea, Haméa, Iaai, Kwênyii, Nêlêmwa, Nemi, Numèè, Paicî, Pije, Xârâcùù, Xârâgurè, Yuanga, Nengone.

sources.citation: Leenhardt 1946, §1-2 of neighbouring southern-group notices (Arhâ p.24, Aro p.29, Boewe p.33, Ciri p.47, Anesù p.53) — read for comparison of how the 'Accent et ton' slot is filled.
sources.note: Same pattern: the accent paragraph is empty or impressionistic for the minor southern languages; the placement rule is given only in the Ajië chapter.

sources.citation: Leenhardt, Maurice. 1946. Langues et dialectes de l'Austro-Mélanésie (Travaux et Mémoires de l'Institut d'Ethnologie 46). Paris: Institut d'Ethnologie. Chapter '5. Sirhë', pp. 38-42 (Gallica ark:/12148/bpt6k21694f, views 85-89).
sources.note: The Sirhë 'Phonétique' has §1 'Mêmes consonnes et voyelles qu'en AJIË, et même valeur' and §2 'Accent et ton', which records only a pitch contrast on a pronoun pair (doa¹ 1pl 'bas' vs doa³ 3pl 'haut et sonore'); no statement of where word stress falls. pp.39-42 (word shapes, particles, pronouns, numerals, verb) add nothing on accent.
Nothing: 19 speakers (ISEE 2009), aire Ajië-Arhö, three short texts (colours, numerals 1-5, plants); no alphabet or phonology notice.
Nothing; stubs citing ALK, UNESCO Atlas and a 2010 Les Nouvelles Calédoniennes article 'Une langue va mourir'.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2012. Change Request 2012-130 [sih] Zire -> Sîshëë. SIL International.
sources.note: Nothing; name-change rationale citing Corpus de la Parole and ALK web pages.

sources.citation: Grace, George W. 1976. Grand Couli Dictionary (New Caledonia). Pacific Linguistics C-12. Canberra: ANU. (closest documented relative, Tîrî; front matter read.)
sources.note: Nothing on Zire; no stress remarks in the introduction.

sources.citation: 'Une langue va mourir', Les Nouvelles Calédoniennes, 19 Nov 2010 (cited by Wikipedia).

sources.citation: Rivierre, Jean-Claude. 2004. Évolution des formes canoniques dans les langues de Nouvelle-Calédonie. Faits de Langues 23-24 (Les langues austronésiennes): 141ff. Paris: Ophrys (now Brill).

sources.note: Pan-New-Caledonian survey of word shape, accent and tone by the areal specialist; the most likely modern place where the prosodic type of Sîchë/Zire (accentual vs tonal, accent position in the southern group) is characterised, which would supersede Leenhardt's impressionistic notice.
